name: 67-unicode
note: The page does not name its character set. wkhtmltopdf assumes an old Western one, so every Greek, Cyrillic and accented letter, maths sign and curly quote comes out garbled (Î±Î²Î³ for αβγ, cafÃ© for café); marqius-wkhtmltopdf prints them as written. name: 70-visibility
note: wkhtmltopdf turns the half-transparent line into a low-resolution picture (96 dots an inch), so it prints blurred and its words cannot be searched or copied; marqius-wkhtmltopdf keeps them as sharp text. The rest of the page is the same.

name: 61-svg-inline

Compare's picture of this page shows marqius-wkhtmltopdf's box flat grey because compare does not draw gradients. Up to 0.12.7, the label, which asks for Helvetica, came out in Times New Roman.

name: 69-borders

name: 71-forms

name: 42-inline-format
note: The first line's words stand up to 1.4 pt along the line from where wkhtmltopdf puts them (subscript and superscript). The pages look the same.

name: certificate
note: wkhtmltopdf writes the letter-spaced title as single letters (it reads back as C E RT IFIC AT E); marqius-wkhtmltopdf keeps the word whole. The pages look the same. Up to 0.12.6, the lines below the title sat 1.2 pt higher.

name: statement

name: javascript

name: notice-he
note: From 0.12.8 the pages look the same. Copied or searched, marqius-wkhtmltopdf's text gives back 43 of the notice's 48 words as written, wkhtmltopdf's 28: it splits many Hebrew words into single letters, which is the text measure's loss. Up to 0.12.7, marqius-wkhtmltopdf drew the letters of each Hebrew word in reverse order and did not mirror the right-to-left table.

name: invoice-ar
note: From 0.12.8 the pages look the same. Copied or searched, marqius-wkhtmltopdf's text gives back 48 of the invoice's 56 words as written, wkhtmltopdf's 2: it stores the Arabic as separate letter shapes, which is most of the text measure's loss. Up to 0.12.7, marqius-wkhtmltopdf drew Arabic letters unjoined and in reverse order, and did not mirror the right-to-left table.

name: letter-hi
note: Both pages look alike. From 0.12.7 marqius-wkhtmltopdf's text reads back as clean Hindi; wkhtmltopdf's does not (16 of its letters have no text at all), which is most of the text measure's loss. Letters joined with र (ra), as in प्रिय and ग्राहक, come out apart, with the halant showing, where wkhtmltopdf joins them. Up to 0.12.6, bold Hindi came out regular (FreeSans, not FreeSans Bold), and neither PDF gave back clean Devanagari text.

name: receipt-th
note: The pages look the same. Copied or searched, marqius-wkhtmltopdf's text comes back as clean Thai from 0.12.7; wkhtmltopdf's has its tone and vowel marks split off. Up to 0.12.6, the bold heading came out regular, and neither PDF gave back clean Thai.

name: greek-russian
note: Up to 0.12.7, marqius-wkhtmltopdf set both floated columns 9.6 pt lower; from 0.12.8 the pages are the same.

name: invoice-zh
note: The pages look the same, but wkhtmltopdf's text has look-alike signs in place of some characters, so a search for the company's name in its PDF finds nothing; marqius-wkhtmltopdf's has the real characters. Up to 0.12.6, the line with the dates broke into three lines with marqius-wkhtmltopdf, two with wkhtmltopdf.

name: letter-ja
note: The pages look the same. wkhtmltopdf sets the text in Noto Sans Mono CJK HK, marqius-wkhtmltopdf in Noto Sans CJK JP, the face lang="ja" asks for; wkhtmltopdf's text reads back with some characters as radicals.

name: mixed-scripts
note: The pages look the same. wkhtmltopdf sets all the Chinese, Japanese and Korean words in Noto Sans CJK HK, marqius-wkhtmltopdf in Noto Sans CJK JP.

name: receipt-ko
note: The pages look the same. The wide space after the time reads back as a different space character in the two PDFs.

name: script-file
note: A real difference: marqius-wkhtmltopdf runs scripts written in the page, but not one the page loads from a file (<script src>), so the delivery note's number, lines and parcel count, which script-file.js writes, are missing.
